 UAPB, FAMU seeking fourth-quarter execution 
 By Tanner Spearman · 
 Sports 
 · 
 October 22, 2026 
 Save Official PDF 
 UAPB running back Jalen Williams makes a long kickoff return as Alabama State safety Zamari Hall chases him down in the second quarter Oct. 17 at Simmons Bank Field at Golden Lion Stadium. The return was called back for a holding penalty. (Pine Bluff Commercial/I.C. Murrell)
 A week ago, both the University of Arkansas at Pine Bluff and Florida A&M came up short in the fourth quarter.
 Late-game execution could be the difference on Saturday (Oct. 24) when UAPB and FAMU meet at Bragg Memorial Stadium in Tallahassee, Fla. The game will kick off at 2 p.m. Central (3 p.m. Eastern) on HBCU GO.
 UAPB coach Alonzo Hampton said the Golden Lions must eliminate the mistakes they made last week, particularly in the red zone.
 “Our offense (has) been one of the top offenses in this conference,” Hampton said. “We moved the ball on everybody. We just made some mistakes. … Our guys gotta understand, man, we don’t have a great margin for error here. So, coaches are putting you in position to be successful. You gotta hone into the details, gotta play with great technique and fundamentals.”
 Both teams threw two interceptions apiece in the fourth quarters of their respective games last week. Alabama State outscored UAPB (3-3, 1-2 SWAC) 7-3 in the fourth quarter of a 21-15 Hornet win, while Jackson State won the fourth 15-0 in its 27-17 comeback against the Rattlers.

 Additionally, UAPB was forced to settle for a field goal despite reaching the 7-yard line, while FAMU (2-5, 1-2) fumbled the ball in its own territory in the fourth.
 The loss to Jackson State marked the fourth straight FAMU game which was decided in the fourth quarter.
 Tennessee State and FAMU were tied entering the fourth on Sept. 19, with Tennessee State winning the final quarter 9-6. The Rattlers trailed Alabama A&M 23-21 entering the fourth a week later but were outscored 17-0 over the final 15 minutes.
 They trailed Alabama State 24-14 entering the fourth on Oct. 9 but won the game by outscoring the Hornets 14-3 down the stretch before giving up a third quarter lead to the Tigers last week.
 FAMU coach Quinn Gray said closing out games in the fourth quarter is largely mental.
 “That’s where we’re trying to get to, having that championship mindset to be able to finish,” Gray said. “That’s what a championship program, ultimately, is able to do. They’re able to finish out games and win those games in the fourth quarter because of the attitude, because of the attention to detail, and then the ability to protect the football.”
 One thing which should work in UAPB’s favor is the run game.
 The Golden Lions rank third in the SWAC in both rushing offense and defense, while the Rattlers rank last in both categories. UAPB averages 206.7 rushing yards per game while holding opponents to 133. FAMU averages 71.7 yards per game while allowing 226.1.
 Gray said the Rattlers need to tackle better against UAPB after each of their past three opponents have rushed for 225 or more yards.
 “It’s about putting our guys in the right situation to make the plays, and ultimately, that’s up to our defensive coordinator, Coach (Ryan) Lewis, to put our guys in those situations to stop the run,” Gray said. “I think we did a good job of bottling up Jackson State there (for the) first three quarters. They got some things going in the fourth a little bit late, but at the end of the day, there’s a steady improvement.”
 The passing game may be more favorable for FAMU. The Rattlers’ offense ranks fifth with UAPB ranking seventh through the air, but the more significant difference is on defense.
 While FAMU ranks seventh at defending the pass, the Golden Lions have allowed a league-high 320.8 passing yards per game. UAPB has done better in its past two games, holding Southern and Alabama State to 154 and 166 yards, respectively, and only allowing one passing touchdown. For context, both Southern and Alabama State were without their original starting quarterbacks.
 Possibly related is the fact UAPB’s defense has sacked opposing quarterbacks 11 times, the fewest of any SWAC team. FAMU has 15 sacks, while Mississippi Valley State leads the league with 22 sacks by its defense.
 Tylan Cole leads UAPB with three sacks for 21 yards, with Keiyhaun Wilks adding 2.5 for eight yards.
 Hampton said he isn’t concerned about those numbers, saying many of the quarterbacks UAPB has faced have been releasing quick, short passes so the pass rushers can’t get to them.
 “They’re getting rid of the ball,” Hampton said. “They’re spreading you out, then you got guys that are able to run the ball and make you be honest. That’ll kind of keep you off from running, chasing the quarterback. So, I think that’s part of it. … Our guys have gotten better. They’re understanding where they need to be. Keep the ball in front.”
 This will be FAMU’s homecoming game, making this the third straight UAPB game where the home team was celebrating homecoming. UAPB had its festivities last week after spoiling Southern’s homecoming the game prior.
